rationale:
Split into 4 children. The supplied proof of this node (Simon 3.7, printed (1)–(5), plus the exhaustion of U) has two kinds of content. One part is specific to varifolds: the good and bad sets, the Besicovitch estimate (printed (2)), and the use of the monotonicity and limit siblings. The other part is four general facts that never mention varifolds. The problem policy requires every new named helper to be its own DAG node, so without a split this node would be one monolithic Lean proof of about 300 lines. The children are exactly those four general facts:
(1) thickening_rel_compact = step 1a. If W ⊂⊂ U, there is ρ₀ > 0 with thickening(ρ₀, W) ⊂⊂ U.
(2) relcompact_exhaustion_ae = Step 2. If μ(Uᶜ) = 0 and, for every W ⊂⊂ U, P holds on W off a μ-null set, then P holds μ-a.e.
(3) bad_interior_null = steps 1d–1e (printed (3) and (5)). Assume (P1), liminf a < ∞, b → 0 and μ_q(Bad_{q,k}) ≤ C k⁻¹ a_q + b_q. Then ⋂_{k≥1} ⋃_i interior ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k} is μ-null. The parent's liminf erratum is kept: only the liminf of a_q is assumed finite.
(4) nearby_good_points = first half of step 1f (printed (4)). If x ∈ W, with W open, lies in no interior ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ, there are y_i → x and q_i → ∞ with y_i ∈ W ∖ Bad_{q_i}.

What stays in this node (the assembly), all taken from the supplied proof:
- Get C from besicovitch_ratio_cover_estimate and (P1) from weight_portmanteau_of_radonConverges.
- Reduce to one W ⊂⊂ U by (2). μ_V(Uᶜ) = 0 follows from Varifold.weight_apply and V.supported.
- Take ρ₀ from (1). For y ∈ W, ball y ρ₀ ⊆ thickening ρ₀ W ⊆ U.
- Define Bad_{i,k} = W ∖ A_{i,k} (printed (1)) and prove printed (2), μ_i(Bad_{i,k}) ≤ C k⁻¹ ‖δV_i‖(W̃) + μ_i(B_i ∩ W), from the Besicovitch sibling (step 1c).
- Apply (3) with a_q = ‖δV_q‖(W̃) and b_q = μ_q(B_q ∩ W) to get the null set E_W.
- For x ∈ W ∖ E_W, unfold membership to get k ≥ 1 with x outside every interior. Apply (4) to Bad_{·,k}. Then apply weight_closedBall_lower_bound_of_density_ge_one at each y_i with Λ = k, and finish with lower_density_ge_one_of_nearby_mass_bounds.
No child depends on another child or on a sibling. No child restates the parent, a sibling, or another DAG node.

subproblems.title: Some uniform thickening of W ⊂⊂ U is still ⊂⊂ U (choice of ρ₀ and W̃ in the proof of 3.7)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^N = Euclidean N be open, and let W ⊆ ℝ^N satisfy W ⊂⊂ U, i.e. IsRelCompactOpenIn W U: W is open, closure W is compact and closure W ⊆ U. Then there is ρ₀ > 0 such that W̃ := thickening(ρ₀, W) = {z ∈ ℝ^N : infEdist(z, W) < ofReal ρ₀} also satisfies W̃ ⊂⊂ U: W̃ is open, closure W̃ is compact and closure W̃ ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclidean N)), IsOpen U → IsRelCompactOpenIn W U → ∃ ρ₀ : ℝ, 0 < ρ₀ ∧ IsRelCompactOpenIn (thickening ρ₀ W) U
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 8, printed proof of 3.7 (p. 212): "take any W ⊂⊂ U and ρ₀ ∈ (0, dist(W, ∂U))" and W̃ = {x : dist(x, W) < ρ₀}. This is step 1a of the parent proof, in a form that also covers U = ℝ^N: no distance to an empty boundary is used.

1. By hypothesis closure W is compact, U is open and closure W ⊆ U. A compact subset of an open set in a (pseudo)metric space has a closed thickening inside the open set (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). So there is δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, closure W) ⊆ U. Put ρ₀ := δ > 0 and W̃ := thickening(ρ₀, W).
2. W̃ is open (isOpen_thickening).
3. closure W̃ ⊆ cthickening(ρ₀, W) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening). Also cthickening(ρ₀, W) = cthickening(ρ₀, closure W) (cthickening_closure), because infEdist(z, W) = infEdist(z, closure W). Hence closure W̃ ⊆ cthickening(ρ₀, closure W) ⊆ U by step 1.
4. ℝ^N is a proper metric space and closure W is compact, so cthickening(ρ₀, closure W) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). closure W̃ is a closed subset of it (step 3), hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
5. Steps 2, 4 and 3 are the three clauses of IsRelCompactOpenIn W̃ U: W̃ is open, closure W̃ is compact, and closure W̃ ⊆ U. Together with ρ₀ > 0 this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open gives δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, closure W) ⊆ U; take ρ₀ = δ.
closure(thickening ρ₀ W) ⊆ cthickening ρ₀ W = cthickening ρ₀ (closure W) ⊆ U.
cthickening ρ₀ (closure W) is compact (proper space), so its closed subset closure(thickening ρ₀ W) is compact.

subproblems.title: Local to global almost everywhere: exhaustion of an open U by countably many balls W ⊂⊂ U
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^N = Euclidean N be open, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, and let P be a property of points of ℝ^N. Suppose that for every W ⊂⊂ U (IsRelCompactOpenIn W U) there is a set E ⊆ ℝ^N, not necessarily measurable, with μ(E) = 0 (outer measure) such that P(x) holds for every x ∈ W with x ∉ E. Then P(x) holds for μ-almost every x ∈ ℝ^N (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, P x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (P : Euclidean N → Prop), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ W : Set (Euclidean N), IsRelCompactOpenIn W U → ∃ E : Set (Euclidean N), μ E = 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ W, x ∉ E → P x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, P x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 (exhaustion) of the parent proof, which is the covering part of STEP 4 of the grandparent proof (root.density_semicontinuity-a1): "Cover U by countably many W ⊂⊂ U". Simon's printed proof of 3.7 leaves this step implicit: it proves the density bound for points of one W ⊂⊂ U off a μ-null set (p. 213, (4)–(5)) and ends with "the theorem is established (by (4))". This lemma passes from all such W to μ-a.e. point. Here μ of an arbitrary set is its outer measure.

1. Radii. Let x ∈ U. As U is open there is ε > 0 with B°_ε(x) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put r_x := ε/2 > 0. Then B_{r_x}(x) ⊆ B°_ε(x) ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_ball, as ε/2 < ε). Choose such r_x for every x ∈ U.
2. The balls are ⊂⊂ U. Let x ∈ U and W_x := B°_{r_x}(x). W_x is open, and closure W_x ⊆ B_{r_x}(x) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). Closed balls of ℝ^N are compact (proper space, isCompact_closedBall), so closure W_x, a closed subset of B_{r_x}(x), is compact. Finally closure W_x ⊆ B_{r_x}(x) ⊆ U by step 1. Hence IsRelCompactOpenIn W_x U.
3. Countable subcover. ℝ^N is second countable. So for the family (W_x)_{x∈U} of open sets, indexed by the subtype U, there is a countable set T ⊆ U of indices with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = ⋃_{x∈U} W_x (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). Every y ∈ U lies in W_y because r_y > 0, so U ⊆ ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = ⋃_{x∈T} W_x.
4. Local exceptional sets. For each x ∈ U apply the hypothesis to W_x (allowed by step 2). Choose E_x ⊆ ℝ^N with μ(E_x) = 0 and P(y) for every y ∈ W_x ∖ E_x.
5. The exceptional set. Let F := {y : ¬P(y)}. Claim: F ⊆ Uᶜ ∪ ⋃_{x∈T} E_x. Let y ∈ F. If y ∉ U, then y ∈ Uᶜ. If y ∈ U, by step 3 there is x ∈ T with y ∈ W_x. If y ∉ E_x, step 4 would give P(y), contradicting y ∈ F. Hence y ∈ E_x ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} E_x.
6. Null. μ(Uᶜ) = 0 by hypothesis. T is countable and μ(E_x) = 0 for all x ∈ T, so μ(⋃_{x∈T} E_x) = 0 by countable subadditivity of the outer measure (measure_biUnion_null_iff). Hence μ(Uᶜ ∪ ⋃_{x∈T} E_x) ≤ μ(Uᶜ) + μ(⋃_{x∈T} E_x) = 0 (measure_union_null). By step 5 and monotonicity, μ(F) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
7. μ({y : ¬P(y)}) = 0 is exactly ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, P y (ae_iff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For x ∈ U choose r_x > 0 with B_{r_x}(x) ⊆ U; W_x := B°_{r_x}(x) is open with compact closure ⊆ B_{r_x}(x) ⊆ U, so W_x ⊂⊂ U.
Second countability (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable): a countable T ⊆ U with U ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} W_x.
The hypothesis on each W_x gives a μ-null E_x with P on W_x ∖ E_x.
{¬P} ⊆ Uᶜ ∪ ⋃_{x∈T} E_x, which is μ-null; hence ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, P y.

subproblems.title: Printed (3) and (5) of the proof of 3.7: the exceptional set ⋂_{k≥1} ⋃_i interior ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k} is μ-null
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let μ and μ_q (q ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, let W ⊆ ℝ^N, let Bad_{q,k} ⊆ ℝ^N (q, k ∈ ℕ) be arbitrary sets with Bad_{q,k} ⊆ W, let C ∈ ℕ, and let a, b : ℕ → [0,∞]. Assume: (P1) μ(O) ≤ liminf_{q→∞} μ_q(O) for every open O ⊆ W; liminf_{q→∞} a_q < ∞; b_q → 0; and μ_q(Bad_{q,k}) ≤ C·k⁻¹·a_q + b_q in [0,∞] for all q ∈ ℕ and all k ≥ 1, where μ_q of an arbitrary set is its outer measure. Then μ(⋂_{k≥1} ⋃_{i∈ℕ} interior(⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k})) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N)) (W : Set (Euclidean N)) (Bad : ℕ → ℕ → Set (Euclidean N)) (C : ℕ) (a b : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞), (∀ O : Set (Euclidean N), IsOpen O → O ⊆ W → μ O ≤ liminf (fun q ↦ μs q O) atTop) → (∀ q k, Bad q k ⊆ W) → liminf a atTop ≠ ∞ → Tendsto b atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ q k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → μs q (Bad q k) ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * (k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ * a q + b q) → μ (⋂ k : ℕ, ⋂ (_ : 1 ≤ k), ⋃ i : ℕ, interior (⋂ ℓ : ℕ, ⋂ (_ : i ≤ ℓ), Bad ℓ k)) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 8, printed proof of 3.7 (pp. 212–213), displays (3) and (5), as filled in by steps 1d–1e of the parent proof. Documented correction: the printed constant "c independent of i, j" is replaced by the liminf bound (only liminf_q a_q < ∞ is assumed), and the bound is taken inside the liminf over q. In the application μ_q = μ_{V_q}, μ = μ_V, a_q = ‖δV_q‖(W̃), b_q = μ_{V_q}(B_q ∩ W), and the hypothesis on μ_q(Bad_{q,k}) is printed (2).

Write L := liminf_q a_q < ∞ and, for i, k ∈ ℕ, O_{i,k} := interior(⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k}).

1. Properties of O_{i,k}.
 (a) O_{i,k} is open.
 (b) For every ℓ ≥ i: O_{i,k} ⊆ ⋂_{ℓ'≥i} Bad_{ℓ',k} ⊆ Bad_{ℓ,k} (interior_subset).
 (c) Taking ℓ = i in (b): O_{i,k} ⊆ Bad_{i,k} ⊆ W.
 (d) If i ≤ i', every ℓ ≥ i' also satisfies ℓ ≥ i, so ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k} ⊆ ⋂_{ℓ≥i'} Bad_{ℓ,k}. Interior is monotone, so O_{i,k} ⊆ O_{i',k}. Thus i ↦ O_{i,k} is increasing.
2. Printed (3): μ(O_{i,k}) ≤ C·k⁻¹·L for every i and every k ≥ 1. Fix such i, k and put c := C·k⁻¹. Since k ≥ 1, k ≠ 0, so k⁻¹ ≠ ∞; also C ≠ ∞. Hence c ≠ ∞.
 (a) By (P1) for the open set O_{i,k} ⊆ W (1a, 1c): μ(O_{i,k}) ≤ liminf_q μ_q(O_{i,k}).
 (b) For every q ≥ i, O_{i,k} ⊆ Bad_{q,k} (1b). By monotonicity and the hypothesis, μ_q(O_{i,k}) ≤ μ_q(Bad_{q,k}) ≤ c·a_q + b_q. This holds for all sufficiently large q, so liminf_q μ_q(O_{i,k}) ≤ liminf_q (c·a_q + b_q) (liminf_le_liminf; in the complete lattice [0,∞] no boundedness side conditions are needed).
 (c) Since b_q → 0, liminf_q (c·a_q + b_q) = liminf_q (c·a_q) (ENNReal.liminf_add_of_right_tendsto_zero).
 (d) Since c ≠ ∞, multiplication by c commutes with liminf: liminf_q (c·a_q) = c·liminf_q a_q = c·L (ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top). Equivalently, use Monotone.map_liminf_of_continuousAt for the monotone map t ↦ c·t, which is continuous by ENNReal.continuous_const_mul.
 Chaining (a)–(d) gives μ(O_{i,k}) ≤ C·k⁻¹·L.
3. Printed (5): μ(E) ≤ C·k⁻¹·L for every k ≥ 1, where E := ⋂_{k≥1} ⋃_i O_{i,k}. Fix k ≥ 1. Then E ⊆ ⋃_i O_{i,k}, so μ(E) ≤ μ(⋃_i O_{i,k}). Since i ↦ O_{i,k} is increasing (1d), continuity from below (Monotone.measure_iUnion) gives μ(⋃_i O_{i,k}) = sup_i μ(O_{i,k}). Each μ(O_{i,k}) ≤ C·k⁻¹·L by step 2, so the supremum is ≤ C·k⁻¹·L.
4. The bound tends to 0. In [0,∞], k⁻¹ → 0 as k → ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero). Since C ≠ ∞, C·k⁻¹ → C·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). Since L ≠ ∞, C·k⁻¹·L → 0·L = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const).
5. Conclusion. By step 3, μ(E) ≤ C·k⁻¹·L for all k ≥ 1, i.e. eventually in k. By step 4 the right side tends to 0, so μ(E) ≤ 0 (ge_of_tendsto), i.e. μ(E) = 0. As E is exactly ⋂_{k≥1} ⋃_{i∈ℕ} interior(⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k}), this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: O_{i,k} := interior ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_{ℓ,k} is open, ⊆ Bad_{ℓ,k} for ℓ ≥ i, ⊆ W, and increasing in i.
Printed (3): μ(O_{i,k}) ≤ liminf_q μ_q(O_{i,k}) ≤ liminf_q (C k⁻¹ a_q + b_q) = liminf_q C k⁻¹ a_q = C k⁻¹ liminf_q a_q.
Printed (5): μ(⋂_k ⋃_i O_{i,k}) ≤ μ(⋃_i O_{i,k}) = sup_i μ(O_{i,k}) ≤ C k⁻¹ L for every k ≥ 1.
C k⁻¹ L → 0 because C, L < ∞, so the set is μ-null.

subproblems.title: Printed (4), first half: points y_i → x and indices q_i → ∞ with y_i ∈ W ∖ Bad_{q_i}
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let W ⊆ ℝ^N = Euclidean N be open, let Bad_ℓ ⊆ ℝ^N (ℓ ∈ ℕ) be arbitrary sets, and let x ∈ W satisfy x ∉ interior(⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ) for every i ∈ ℕ. Then there are q : ℕ → ℕ and y : ℕ → ℝ^N with q_i → ∞ and y_i → x as i → ∞, such that y_i ∈ W and y_i ∉ Bad_{q_i} for every i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclidean N)) (Bad : ℕ → Set (Euclidean N)) (x : Euclidean N), IsOpen W → x ∈ W → (∀ i : ℕ, x ∉ interior (⋂ ℓ : ℕ, ⋂ (_ : i ≤ ℓ), Bad ℓ)) → ∃ (q : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℕ → Euclidean N), Tendsto q atTop atTop ∧ Tendsto y atTop (𝓝 x) ∧ ∀ i, y i ∈ W ∧ y i ∉ Bad (q i)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 8, printed proof of 3.7, p. 212, the sentences before display (4): "consider the possibility that there is a point x ∈ W such that x ∈ W ∖ interior ⋂_{q≥i} B_{q,j} for each i. Then we could select, for each i, y_i ∈ W ∖ ⋂_{q≥i} B_{q,j} with |y_i − x| < 1/i. Thus there are sequences y_i → x and q_i → ∞ such that y_i ∉ B_{q_i,j}." This is the "Choice of y_i, q_i" in step 1f of the parent proof, with Bad_ℓ = Bad_{ℓ,k} for the fixed k. The radius is 1/(i+1) because i starts at 0.

1. Fix i ∈ ℕ and let G_i := W ∩ B°_{1/(i+1)}(x). G_i is open, as the intersection of the open set W and an open ball. And x ∈ G_i, because x ∈ W and dist(x, x) = 0 < 1/(i+1).
2. Claim: there are ℓ ∈ ℕ and z ∈ ℝ^N with i ≤ ℓ, z ∈ W, dist(z, x) < 1/(i+1) and z ∉ Bad_ℓ. Suppose not. Then every z ∈ G_i satisfies z ∈ Bad_ℓ for all ℓ ≥ i, i.e. G_i ⊆ ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ. Since G_i is open, G_i ⊆ interior(⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ) (interior_maximal). So x ∈ interior(⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ) by step 1, contradicting the hypothesis for this i.
3. By step 2 and the axiom of choice there are q : ℕ → ℕ and y : ℕ → ℝ^N such that, for every i: i ≤ q_i, y_i ∈ W, dist(y_i, x) < 1/(i+1) and y_i ∉ Bad_{q_i}.
4. q_i → ∞: q_i ≥ i for every i, and i → ∞ (tendsto_atTop_mono with the identity).
5. y_i → x: 0 ≤ dist(y_i, x) ≤ 1/(i+1), and 1/(i+1) → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat). So dist(y_i, x) → 0 by the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero), which means y_i → x (tendsto_iff_dist_tendsto_zero).
6. Steps 3–5 give q and y with all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: G_i := W ∩ B°_{1/(i+1)}(x) is an open neighbourhood of x.
If G_i ⊆ ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ then x ∈ interior ⋂_{ℓ≥i} Bad_ℓ (interior_maximal), a contradiction; so there are y_i ∈ G_i and q_i ≥ i with y_i ∉ Bad_{q_i}.
Choose y_i, q_i for every i; q_i ≥ i gives q_i → ∞.
